04Reading the tracks

Dates hold different meanings.

History and poetry share an axis, but their dates describe different things. A poem’s composition, publication, and English translation may be years apart. Approximate dates remain approximate; spans mark events that unfold over time.

August 1947 has its own detail view. Independence celebrations on August 14–15 and the boundary announcement on August 17 are separate moments. Faiz’s poem is dated only to August, so its marker belongs to the whole month.

An exhibit in progress.

Each card identifies its references and any open editorial questions. Unverified first-publication dates, translations, and individual poem selections are explicitly marked. “Freedom’s Dawn” is presented in V. G. Kiernan’s English translation. Other poem selections remain in progress.

Portraits are displayed in monochrome with a crop for consistent framing. Each portrait links to its source and reuse terms; credited images retain their stated licenses.
